title: Equal Steps: Arithmetic Progression Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Aarav puts 50 rupees in a jar in week one and adds 20 rupees every week after that. How much will be in the jar after a whole year, without counting week by week? In this animated lesson on NCERT Chapter 8, Sequences and Series, we meet the arithmetic progression (A P) and its one line formula.

You will watch the weekly savings grow as bars, one equal step at a time, while n counts up and the tops line up in a straight line. Fence posts and gaps show why the nth term needs n - 1 steps, and we build an = a + (n - 1)d in small steps. Then rising and falling A Ps side by side, the A P test by subtraction, Aarav's 52-week answer, the exam trap of using n steps instead of n - 1, and an original JEE Main pattern question. A recap card and three questions to check yourself close the lesson.

Note: arithmetic progressions are taught in the NCERT Class 10 book and are not in the current (rationalised) Class 11 NCERT text, but they are in the JEE Main syllabus.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
